sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and applicable European Union internal-market rules
France-China Agreement on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, signed 10 March 2007 and in force subject to its terms
France-China Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed 26 November 2013 and in force
Applicable French bilateral double-taxation treaties with the country of residence of each shareholder, director, beneficial owner, supplier, or financing party
Applicable European Union customs, VAT, sanctions, AML, consumer-protection, and digital-services legislation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT obligations are principally governed by the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and related regulatory provisions, including Articles R.561-1 to R.561-22-1. Beneficial-owner identification and filing obligations for companies are principally governed by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and Articles R.561-1 to R.561-3 of that Code, together with Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 concerning the register of beneficial owners and subsequent amendments. Commercial registration is administered through the Registre National des Entreprises under Law No. 2019-486 of 22 May 2019 and related implementing provisions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or current commercial-register extract of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or companies authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing country is a Hague Apostille Convention party; otherwise consular legalization through the issuing authority, the competent foreign ministry, and the relevant French consulate, unless a treaty exemption applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Current articles of association and constitutional documents of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, notary, or competent authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, as applicable; certified French translation may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or shareholder resolution approving the French investment and appointing the authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder or its competent governing body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization where required by the country of origin, followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified French translation may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation, filing, and formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder, proposed manager, or authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization where required, followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; French translation may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity document of each individual shareholder, manager, authorized signatory, and identified beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national identity-card issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy or professional certification; apostille or consular legalization is generally not required for a valid passport copy unless requested by the receiving institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each manager and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, public authority, bank, or other accepted issuer in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy, with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization only where requested by the registry, bank, notary, or regulated service provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French company, its legal representative, and the relevant corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Filed through the French business-formality system; underlying foreign corporate records must follow the applicable apostille or consular-legalization route

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence or equivalent tax-status evidence, where treaty or banking analysis requires it
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the relevant country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where required by the recipient or applicable treaty practice

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and continuously thereafter, screen the company, managers, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, principal suppliers, payment counterparties, and relevant intermediaries against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union financial-sanctions lists, French national sanctions measures, applicable United States OFAC lists, and other risk-relevant national lists. Conduct PEP, family-member, close-associate, adverse-media, corruption, fraud, terrorist-financing, proliferation-financing, and high-risk-country screening. Apply enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, source-of-funds verification, and enhanced transaction monitoring for PEPs, sanctioned-country exposure, opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, unexplained virtual assets, high-risk payment corridors, or adverse media. Do not process prohibited transactions or make funds available to designated persons. Retain AML records for the statutory period, generally five years under the French Monetary and Financial Code, subject to applicable extended requirements.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_determination_method: Identify every natural person who directly or indirectly holds more than 25 percent of the capital or voting rights, or exercises control by any other means, including control over governing bodies or decision-making. If no natural person is identifiable after reasonable investigation, identify the legal representative or equivalent senior managing officer in accordance with French law. Trace ownership through every intermediate entity and document the calculation of indirect ownership and voting rights.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_register_access_position: Beneficial-owner information is filed with the competent French register and is available to competent authorities, AML-obliged professionals, and other persons with legally recognized access. Public access is restricted following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment in Case C-37/20 and C-601/20 and subsequent French and European implementation measures. Access may require an identified legitimate interest or statutory entitlement.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.nominee_and_layered_ownership_controls: Nominee shareholders, undisclosed agency arrangements, bearer-share structures, unexplained trusts, and layered ownership without a documented commercial rationale present heightened AML risk. The company must obtain documentary evidence of legal ownership, control rights, shareholder agreements, voting arrangements, fiduciary relationships, and the ultimate source of funds before accepting the investment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with company data recorded in the Registre National des Entreprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_clearance_method: France has no general statutory company-name reservation system equivalent to a 30-day reserved-name certificate. Conduct clearance through the INPI name and business database, the Registre National des Entreprises, the Institut national de la propriété industrielle trademark database, the EUIPO database, domain-name searches, and commercial-name searches. Name availability is not a guarantee against later trademark, trade-name, unfair-competition, or passing-off claims.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A French SARL may generally use a French or foreign-language corporate name. There is no general statutory requirement that the name be written in French or in a local non-Latin script. The name must be distinctive enough to avoid confusion, must not be misleading, and must comply with public-order, trademark, consumer-protection, and regulated-activity rules. Corporate documents and filings are generally prepared in French; foreign-language supporting documents may require a translation by a translator accepted by French authorities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: University and other protected public-service or professional designations
Any term suggesting a public authority, licensed profession, regulated financial activity, or government affiliation without the required authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Because no general statutory reservation period exists, obtain written confirmation of any provisional hold directly from the filing agent or platform and do not treat it as a legal monopoly. If a filing is rejected, obtain the written rejection reason, correct the proposed name or supporting evidence, and resubmit through the INPI Guichet unique. If the rejection constitutes an administrative decision that remains disputed, request reconsideration from the competent registry or authority and, where appropriate, file a judicial challenge before the competent commercial court or an administrative challenge before the competent administrative court within the applicable time limit stated in the decision. Separately assess trademark opposition, cancellation, or infringement exposure before adopting the name.
recommended_clearance_sequence: Search the Registre National des Entreprises and INPI corporate-name resources
Search French, European Union, and relevant international trademark databases
Search domain names, trade names, business signs, and major marketplace identifiers
Check regulated-word restrictions and obtain any required ministerial or regulatory consent
Prepare a written name-risk opinion and reserve matching domains and social-media identifiers
Use the legal name consistently on incorporation documents, invoices, websites, contracts, and payment accounts

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_basis: A French SARL must have a registered office in France and disclose that address in its constitutional documents and registration filing. The registered office may be located at premises owned or occupied by the company, at the manager's residence subject to statutory conditions, or with a qualified domiciliation provider under the French Commercial Code, including Articles L.123-11-1 et seq. and related provisions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for a B2B electronic wholesale marketplace if it is a lawful domiciliation arrangement with an authorized provider, includes a written domiciliation contract, permits receipt of official correspondence, and satisfies provider identification, premises, record-keeping, and inspection-access requirements. A mailbox-only address, unverifiable premises, or address masking the actual management and operational location is unsuitable. The business should maintain operational records, contracts, accounting records, customer and supplier files, and decision-making evidence in accordance with tax, AML, and commercial requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated unannounced physical-inspection risk: 5% to 15% during the first two years for a standard low-risk B2B platform with a compliant domiciliation provider, increasing materially if the company has high-risk jurisdictions, unusual payment flows, customs anomalies, consumer complaints, tax inconsistencies, sanctions indicators, or an unverifiable office. This is a risk estimate, not an official French government statistic.
commercial_substance_requirements: Appoint a real French-resident or otherwise legally eligible manager with documented authority and contact details
Maintain a functioning registered office capable of receiving official communications
Maintain accurate accounting records and tax documentation
Document platform contracts, supplier onboarding, customer verification, payment flows, refunds, and complaints
Maintain VAT, customs, product-compliance, and cross-border transaction records
Use a bank or payment institution whose AML file is consistent with the declared business model
Avoid presenting a nominal registered office as the sole location of substantive management where management actually occurs elsewhere
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.industry_specific_observations: The stated B2B marketplace activity generally does not require a general statutory business licence merely to operate an electronic wholesale platform. Separate requirements may arise for payment services, electronic money, consumer sales, regulated goods, imports, product safety, data protection, cybersecurity, customs representation, and platform activities conducted for consumers. The company must not hold client funds or provide regulated payment services without the applicable authorization or licensed payment partner.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI Guichet unique incorporation filing and registry charges for a commercial SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French business-formality system, commercial registry, and associated registry service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory and registry tariffs; exact amount varies with current tariff schedule and filing characteristics

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French commercial registry or INPI filing system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or registry tariff, subject to current schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal notice of incorporation in an authorized journal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated annual or departmental tariff, depending on notice length and location
Prevailing market benchmark; price varies by city, mail handling, meeting facilities, and compliance services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation or review of SARL articles, manager appointment, shareholder resolutions, and incorporation documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French corporate counsel or incorporation professional
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; not generally a statutory fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO tracing, ownership chart, AML onboarding, sanctions screening, and source-of-funds review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French counsel, AML provider, or regulated corporate-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark based on ownership complexity and number of jurisdictions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign corporate-record certification, notarization, apostille, or consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary, competent authority, apostille authority, foreign ministry, and/or French consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official authentication charges plus local professional fees; highly jurisdiction-dependent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn or certified French translations of foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French sworn translator or translator accepted by the receiving authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, commonly calculated by page, word count, or document complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate-name, trademark, domain, trade-name, and regulated-token clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French or European trademark counsel and domain registrars
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; official trademark filing fees are excluded unless a filing is requested

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French bank or payment-institution onboarding and compliance file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Bank, payment institution, or authorized payment-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provider-specific onboarding, account, and compliance charges; many institutions charge no initial fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial accounting, VAT, and cross-border transaction assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French chartered accountant or tax adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; scope depends on VAT registrations, customs, marketplace flows, and reporting volume

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, consular handling, courier, and document-certification contingencies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Variable official charges and market costs

pre_incorporation_compliance_conditions: Confirm the identity, nationality, residence, tax residence, source of wealth, source of funds, and sanctions status of all shareholders, managers, signatories, and beneficial owners.

Confirm that the proposed B2B marketplace will not conduct payment services, electronic-money issuance, lending, insurance distribution, investment services, or custody of client funds without the required authorization.

Determine whether the platform acts as principal, undisclosed agent, commissionaire, marketplace intermediary, importer, or customs declarant, because the characterization affects VAT, customs, contractual, and product-liability exposure.
Assess GDPR, e-commerce, cybersecurity, data-transfer, platform-governance, product-safety, unfair-commercial-practice, and electronic-contract requirements before launch.
Document the registered-office arrangement, French management nexus, accounting location, bank or payment-provider relationship, and operational substance.
Verify the availability and enforceability of the chosen company name independently from registry acceptance.
File changes to beneficial ownership, managers, registered office, shareholding, or control promptly within the applicable French filing periods.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9, L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL); Civil Code Articles 1832 to 1844-9; Décret n° 2007-431 on the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; filings submitted through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) incorporation application via electronic Cerfa n° 15784*02, together with the articles of association, declaration of subscription and payment, and capital deposit certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The French Commercial Code imposes no minimum share capital for a SARL, but cash contributions must be subscribed in full and paid up to at least 20% at incorporation; the balance may be paid within five years. Contributions must be deposited on a blocked bank, notarial, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations account in the name of the company in formation, and the funds are released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribing founders approve the final articles of association and irrevocably subscribe in full the share capital, divided into [X] shares of €[Y] each, with cash contributions paid to the legally required minimum and the balance payable within the statutory term. RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at [Paris address], France. RESOLVED, that [name] be and is hereby appointed gérant, vested with full powers to represent the company, open bank accounts, and complete all incorporation filings. RESOLVED, that the gérant shall, without delay, publish the legal notice and file the incorporation application with the Guichet Unique and the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation articles drafting and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public and/or a regulated bank in France acting as depository
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of association containing the corporate name, registered office address, share capital, share allocation, management, and duration. Open a blocked account at a bank, notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations in the name of the SARL en formation. Deposit the cash contributions and obtain the capital deposit certificate and declaration of subscription and payment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depository rejects the deposit, correct the KYC documentation, select another approved depository, and amend the articles if the share allocation changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Landlord, managed property provider, or commercial domiciliation company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conclude an occupancy lease or domiciliation agreement providing a genuine physical or managed presence in France. Obtain the landlord’s written consent if the registered office is not owned by the company, and retain proof of address for the RCS file.
required_dossiers: Proof of address or attestation from the domiciliation provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe considers the address insufficient, replace it with a registered commercial domiciliation company approved by the local commercial court and submit the revised proof.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal constitution notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal notice journal (Journal d'annonces légales) authorized for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place a formal notice in an approved legal journal containing the proposed company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, gérant identity, and the court where the RCS filing will be made. Obtain the attestation or original newspaper page as proof of publication.
required_dossiers: Project of the articles of association
Proof of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains an error, arrange a corrective publication and attach the corrected attestation to the incorporation file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of articles and appointment of the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the final articles of association by all shareholders, either physically or by electronic signature. Have the proposed gérant sign the acceptance of office. Ensure powers of attorney are attached where any shareholder is represented.
required_dossiers: Acceptance of office signed by the gérant
Power of attorney for any represented shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Missing signatures and incomplete pages are cured by executing a supplementary act or by obtaining fresh signatures from all parties before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic M0 filing with the Guichet Unique and RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, complete the electronic M0/Cerfa 15784*02 form for a SARL, upload all incorporated documents, pay the filing fees, and submit the file. The greffe transmits the approved data to INSEE for SIREN/SIRET assignment.
required_dossiers: Proof of domiciliation and landlord consent
Identity documents of the gérant and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues a query or irregularity notice, correct the file electronically within the stated period, usually fifteen days; unresolved objections may be challenged before the tribunal de commerce or by refiling a compliant application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE, DGFiP, and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, retrieve the Kbis extract, SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and the French tax registration references. Verify that the Guichet Unique has transmitted formation data to the tax and social authorities; if employees will be hired, complete the URSSAF employer registration and any workplace health filing.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract obtained from the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Delayed or missing administrative notifications are corrected by contacting the greffe and using the secure Espace personnel on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr to trigger retransmission to INSEE, DGFiP, or URSSAF.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for an electronic B2B marketplace under ISIC 4791; no industrial licensing board is competent absent a physical manufacturing establishment. If a logistics warehouse is later added, the Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités and the local préfecture may become competent under ICPE rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No regulated statutory operating licence is required for a pure online wholesale platform; the RCS registration and Kbis extract are the sufficient trading credentials under French commercial law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement and the préfecture of the registered office department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure office-based e-commerce; any future warehouse will require an ICPE declaration or authorization under rubrique 1510 if storage capacity thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or point-source emissions arise from standard B2B marketplace operations; any subsequent storage activity must satisfy the wastewater discharge limits of Code de l'environnement Articles R.214-1 et seq. and applicable fire-water retention standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspection are not required for a non-ERP office-based platform. The employer must still comply with workplace health and safety rules under the Code du travail; if the office is open to the public or a warehouse is operated, the appropriate ERP fire authorization and structural clearance must be obtained from the mairie or préfecture.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal and the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Customs export formalities are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through douane.gouv.fr and the DELTA customs systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is incorporated and registered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The registration produces an SIREN identifier for the legal entity and an SIRET identifier for each establishment. The entity must then activate its professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr and register with its competent SIE. The SIE determines the applicable VAT regime and issues or validates the French intra-Community VAT identification number, generally consisting of the FR country code, a two-character key, and the SIREN number. A non-established foreign taxable person must register with the relevant French foreign-business tax service where it makes taxable French supplies that are not fully reverse-charged. The application normally requires constitutional documents, proof of legal existence, identification of directors and beneficial owners, business activity details, French establishment or representative information where applicable, expected turnover, banking information, and evidence supporting the VAT liability. EU-established businesses may generally use the EU VAT registration and One Stop Shop mechanisms where legally available; non-EU businesses may require a French tax representative unless an applicable exemption or reverse-charge rule applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). An eligible SARL may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, or IR), generally subject to statutory conditions concerning age, ownership, activity, employee headcount, turnover or balance-sheet limits, and duration. A qualifying family SARL may elect IR without the same five-year limitation, subject to the family-ownership conditions. France does not operate a United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive provisions and can deny deductions, defer deductions, or impose inclusion where instruments or entities produce deductible/non-included or duplicate deduction outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), with customs duties and import VAT administered separately by the DGDDI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business eligible for the franchise in base, the principal turnover thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and certain related activities and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory tolerance thresholds, activity-specific rules, and legislative amendments. A B2B electronic marketplace may fall within the services threshold depending on its contractual remuneration and supply characterization. There is no general turnover threshold that protects a French-established business from VAT registration once it elects or is required to use a normal VAT regime. A non-established supplier generally has no broad French threshold for taxable French transactions, subject to reverse-charge rules. Intra-Community distance sales of goods and certain electronically supplied services are subject to the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold, after which the destination principle applies, with OSS available for qualifying supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices; large and medium-sized businesses must generally issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from that date. Small and medium-sized businesses, including most SARLs, are generally scheduled to issue them from 1 September 2027. Invoices must be transmitted through an approved private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, or PDP); the public invoicing portal is being used as the government platform infrastructure. Cross-border B2B transactions, B2C transactions, and certain non-domestic flows are subject to e-reporting rather than domestic B2B invoice transmission. France is not based on universal real-time pre-clearance of every invoice; mandatory structured data transmission, platform routing, authenticity and integrity controls, and digital archival requirements apply. The required structured formats and data fields are prescribed by French VAT and e-invoicing regulations and may include transaction, payment, customer identification, VAT, and collection-status data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT when the supplier is the exporter or acts under an applicable export arrangement and can substantiate customs exit from the EU. The supplier must retain the export customs declaration and reliable evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt from French VAT where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier retains transport and customer-VAT evidence and makes required recapitulative statements. Services supplied to a business established outside France are generally governed by place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT rather than technically zero-rated; services connected with French immovable property, events, passenger transport, short-term vehicle hire, and other special categories require separate analysis. A marketplace operator must also assess deemed-supplier rules for platforms facilitating certain B2C imported or intra-EU goods transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration submitted through the applicable DELTA system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic proof that the goods exited the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, air waybill, road consignment note, courier record, or carrier delivery confirmation
Packing list and, where relevant, proof of export authorization, licenses, or restrictions compliance
Customer order, contract, marketplace transaction record, and proof of delivery where relevant
Payment evidence or other commercial evidence supporting the transaction; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory French VAT export document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not generally impose a universal 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline as a condition for export VAT exemption or refund. Export VAT treatment is primarily substantiated by customs exit evidence, transport records, commercial documentation, and transaction consistency. If zero-rating or exemption is unsupported, the DGFiP may reassess output VAT, deny or claw back an input VAT refund, apply late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, and impose tax penalties. The principal penalty rates can include 10% for late or insufficient compliance, 40% for deliberate misconduct, and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. False documentation, concealed transactions, or intentional VAT fraud may also trigger criminal proceedings, including imprisonment and substantial fines under the French Tax Code. Repeated or material non-compliance may result in enhanced audit scrutiny, refusal of refund claims, customs enforcement, and recovery of reassessed VAT, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France — the French central bank, together with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the prudential licensing authority and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) acting as the competent authority for balance-of-payments reporting and exchange-control notifications under the Code monétaire et financier and EU capital-movement rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the euro for both current-account and capital-account transactions, consistent with Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the French Monetary and Financial Code. Capital injections into an SARL by non-resident shareholders, profit distributions, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds may be freely converted and remitted abroad without prior foreign-exchange licensing or central bank approval. The only operational requirements are standard bank KYC/AML checks, sanctions screening, and, where applicable, statistical balance-of-payments declaration to the Banque de France for individual transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 in the non-EU reporting file. There is no restriction on profit remittance, no requirement to obtain an exchange-control certificate, and no discriminatory conversion premium for non-resident owners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory minimum conversion obligations on export proceeds. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in foreign-currency bank accounts held with EU or EEA credit institutions without any conversion requirement. The effitive mandatory conversion ratio is 0%. The only compliance obligations are (i) a statistical reporting duty to the Banque de France for each non-EU foreign-exchange transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000, (ii) inclusion of foreign-currency account balances and receivables in the annual French balance-of-payments statement, and (iii) declaration of any foreign bank account to the French tax administration on the annual tax return (form No. 3916-bis). There is no statutory deadline for converting export receipts; dealers may hold indefinite open positions, subject to normal corporate treasury and transfer-pricing policies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for operational accounts and EUR payment collection, Medium for cross-border multi-currency disbursement, and Low for capital-escrow services and documentary-credit instruments. Regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) authorised in France under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2) — e.g., Qonto, Shine, Lydia Solutions, and Manager — may open fully digital account structures for an SARL without physical branch visits. However, a French-licensed EMI cannot hold an escrow account that requires credit-worthy custody, cannot issue or receive commercial letters of credit, and, when passporting into France from another EEA state, must comply with ACPR passport-notification requirements. For the B2B marketplace model, EMIs are viable as the primary ‘collection rail’ for seller payouts and charge payments, but a traditional credit institution with SWIFT and LC capability remains mandatory for inbound equity capital and large trade-sponsored transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a mandatory physical appearance of directors for account opening; the AML/KYC obligation under the Code monétaire et financier and EU AML directives requires the bank to identify the client and the beneficial owner using reliable, independent source documents. In practice, Tier-1 French banks will generally require at least one face-to-face meeting for non-resident directors unless the bank has a dedicated international remote-onboarding desk. If the director is an EU resident, certified copies of the passport and proof of residence can be accepted; if the director is from a non-EOA high-risk jurisdiction, physical presence or an apostilled and notarised power of attorney is almost always demanded. Regulated EMIs allow full remote onboarding subject to video identification, but a traditional bank reserve the right to request a meeting based on the risk profile of the foreign ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain: indirect ownership through trusts, foundations, or entities in non-cooperative jurisdictions without a clear tax rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) filing confirmation prior to the bank application; a shareholding transparency chart in French with all intermediary structures; certified copies of constitutive documents, trust deeds, and shareholder registers; notarised and apostilled declarations identifying each natural-person UBO together with tax residence, national identification number, and residential address; and a covering legal memorandum from the corporate counsel explaining the underlying commercial purpose of any offshore layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and managers without French residential or business presence, triggering substance and ‘shell company’ concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French Kbis extract showing a fully registered SARL registered office; a lease agreement or service contract for the registered premises; the manager's police/identity record and proof of physical address (utility bill less than 3 months old) from the state of residence; a statement of the manager's authority and biographical evidence of genuine operational responsibility; and, where the manager is not in France, an apostilled copy of the employment-supervision agreement or management services agreement with the French entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border B2B marketplace model involving a large number of unrated vendors or payments to jurisdictions with weak AML controls
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan in French explaining the platform marketplace structure; the KYC policy manual for onboarded suppliers, including identification, sanctions screening (OFAC and EU consolidated list), and transaction-monitoring systems; the list of target vendor countries with AML/CFT risk assessment; samples of vendor onboarding files stripped of live data; and an independent audit report or signed management assurance that no vendor has been unverified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds ambiguity for the initial capital contribution, especially when contributions come from personal accounts of foreign shareholders or from a jurisdiction with FATF deficiencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder bank accounts and payment receipts for the preceding 12 months; a written source-of-wealth explanation in French, including employment history, income tax returns, inheritance documents, sale proceeds, or dividends; an independent wealth extract or investment portfolio statement; and an irrevocable instruction that the capital injection is funded exclusively from the personal bank account of the subscribing shareholder and not from any third-party cash or crypto exchange.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing French tax filing history or failure to indicate SIRET, TVA (VAT) registration, and tax-identification details, leading the bank to perceive the entity as a dormant conduit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French SIREN/SIRET registration certificate; VAT identification confirmation from the Centre des Finances Publiques or EDI; copy of the annual statutory financial statements or an opening balance sheet filed with the registre du commerce; employer registration with URSSAF (if any employees); and a certificate from the comptable showing no outstanding tax writes; all documents in French or professionally translated and certified.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing of the SARL capital injection or shareholder loan from abroad must use the SWIFT MT103 payment message, dictating a purpose code of 'D' (direct investment/deposit) or the ISO20022 payment description 'Carbon and equity investment' as instructed by the receiving French bank; the bank requires the exact corporate registration number (SIREN of the SARL) and the underlying equity constitution document. The injection must originate from the shareholder's own bank account in a jurisdiction from which EEA banks accept clear AML evidence, and not from an unrelated third party. If the amount exceeds EUR 50,000, the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical return (remise de déclaration Cotes) must be filed by the bank or the entity within twoworking days; capital movements above EUR 12.5M may trigger additional statistical thresholds. For a foreign-currency injection, the euros are converted at the ECB euro foreign-exchange reference rate prevailing on the valuation date, with the foreign-exchange gain or loss being recognised in the SARL's share premium reserve; no prior approval is required for the conversion. To avoid misclassification as commercial turnover, the account must be earmarked as a separate ‘capital account’ or ‘compte courant d’associé’ and the contribution evidenced by a notarial declaration of subscription and payment, a formal board resolution, and a bank credit advice referencing the corporate identifier.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements from the French SARL for B2B marketplace procurement use four permitted clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 wire transfer for EUR, USD, GBP, or any convertible-currency settlement to suppliers abroad, carrying the purpose code of commercial credit; (2) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (LC) governed by UCP 600, initiated via SWIFT MT700/MT760 through an issuing French bank and a confirming bank abroad, for high-value or sovereign-risk purchases; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for euro payments to EEA suppliers with the shortest clearing cycles and mandatory IBAN identification; and (4) e-commerce/payment institution rails such as Alibaba Pay or Payoneer for catalogue purchases where the transaction value is low, subject to the bank’s pre-approval of counterparty and daily transaction volume. Each outbound disbursement must be supported by a commercial invoice, purchase order, logistics document, or platform supplier contract, and must not be sent to a country subject to European Union sanctions. The bank may require a economic-beneficiary declaration and the provision of the supplier's legal identity and tax number for high-risk corridors; for payments above EUR 50,000 to suppliers outside the EEA, the Banque de France statistical declaration is transmitted automatically by the bank without stopping the payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign exchange spot transactions (câbles/echange comptant) for immediate EUR/USD or EUR/CNY conversion at market rate
Plain-vanilla forward exchange contracts (achat à terme) with maturities generally from one week up to 12 months for firm EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility, including offshore CNY (CNH) and selected emerging-market currencies, contracted in London or Paris only when the SARL has a lawful underlying commercial exposure
FX swaps (swap de change) combining a spot and a forward leg for short-term treasury liquidity management
Currency options, both call and put, purchased with premium payment (options asymétriques) to establish a defined maximum exchange cost without obligating settlement
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) to swap EUR-denominated debt into USD obligations over a multi-year tenor for long-duration financing
Listed FX futures traded on regulated venues such as Euronext or equal EEA exchanges for standardised hedging of inventory exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) incl. balance sheet, income statement, notes, management report, and statutory auditor's report if any
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI Guichet Unique (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval of annual accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; filing with the commercial registry within 1 month after approval. For a calendar-year-end SARL, practical deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered injunction (astreinte) plus administrative fine up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 3,000 on repeat default); continued failure triggers judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and loss of legal good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax annual return (déclaration de résultats n°2065-SD and annexed schedules, liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — electronic filing via EFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December: 3rd business day after 1 May (typically 3/4 May). For off-calendar fiscal years: within 3 months of the fiscal year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus monthly 0.40% late-payment interest; 40% penalty for deliberate omission or false declarations; automatic assessment (taxation d'office) if no return is filed within 30 days of formal demand.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owners annual verification and updated declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI Guichet Unique (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual renewal; update required within 30 days after any event changing beneficial ownership (e.g., share transfer). Verify annually during the accounts-approval cycle and file updates when applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 7,500 per defaulting director plus court order to regularize; false declaration may attract criminal penalties; sustained non-disclosure exposes the entity to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property contribution declaration (cotisation foncière des entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration filed electronically by 15 December for the current year's principal; initial registration declaration within 1 month of commencement of taxable activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus 0.20% monthly interest; automatic tax base assessment in case of non-declaration; persistent arrears may trigger enforced recovery against the SARL's assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when the SARL exceeds two of the three following thresholds: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excl. VAT > EUR 8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Also mandatory for SARLs in a group consolidation or upon application by shareholders holding at least 10% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation 2014-03 as updated) for the SARL's individual statutory accounts under Articles L.123-12 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; IFRS applies only to consolidated group financial statements of the ultimate parent, not to the SARL standalone accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law requires the SARL to maintain an up-to-date beneficial owner declaration at the RCS. The annual protocol: (i) review shareholding/control changes during the fiscal year; (ii) file any corrected or updated declaration via the INPI Guichet Unique within 30 days of each change; (iii) at each annual accounts cycle, confirm that the registry details remain accurate; (iv) keep the signed internal UBO register on site. No separate statutory annual filing exists beyond the update obligation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholder Decisions and Meeting Minutes (Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux d'assemblées)
Minute Book (dossier des procès-verbaux incl. attendance sheets)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 330 – USD 2,700 per year (typical EUR 300 – EUR 2,500 range for registered-office or RCS correspondence-agent services in France)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 – USD 16,500 per year for a statutory audit of a medium-size SARL; micro SARLs below audit thresholds typically incur no audit fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate); 15% reduced rate on the first €42,500 of annual taxable profit for SMEs with turnover < €10 million
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CIR 30% research tax credit; CII 20% innovation tax credit; reduced 15% SME bracket; JEI 100%/50% exemptions; 3.3% social surcharge on IS only where annual IS exceeds €763,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_note: Carryforward is unlimited in time under CGI art. 209, but each year's utilisation is capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding €1,000,000; 1-year carryback available on the first €1,000,000 of loss.
